findings.title: New getShortcut() method breaks existing grant factories at startup
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an existing SPI, and getShortcut() was added as an abstract method with no default. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit casts every OAuth2GrantType factory and calls getShortcut() while building the shortcut maps. A custom grant factory compiled against the previous interface will throw AbstractMethodError during that postInit, which aborts Keycloak startup rather than only disabling that grant. Add a default implementation and treat a missing or null shortcut as unknown so already-deployed grant providers keep the server bootable.

findings.title: Access-token ID matcher rejects a matching grant and checks the wrong slice
findings.body: isAccessTokenId is what the updated CODE_TO_TOKEN, refresh, device, and CIBA event assertions now use, but matchesSafely is inverted and off by one. Encoded IDs are six characters before the colon: session type at 0-1, token type at 2-3, grant type at 4-5 (for example onrtac:<uuid>). The check uses substring(3, 5), which is the last character of the token-type shortcut plus the first character of the grant shortcut, and returns false when that slice equals the expected shortcut. For a correct ID the wrong slice does not equal the expected shortcut, so the method falls through and only checks that the suffix looks like a UUID. Integration tests therefore pass for any <prefix>:<uuid>, including a wrong grant shortcut or the na fallback, and they never check session type or token type. A prefix shorter than 5 characters also throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException out of the matcher instead of failing the match. The condition needs to require a 6-character prefix and compare substring(4, 6) to the expected shortcut.

findings.title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice and allows a null raw token ID
findings.body: The fourth Objects.requireNonNull call passes grantType again, with the message "Null rawTokenId not allowed", instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is stored. encodeTokenId then concatenates it, and Java string conversion turns that into the literal suffix "null" (for example onrtac:null). Every such token shares the same jti, so revocation, event correlation, and replay checks that key on token ID collapse together. The check must be Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...).

findings.title: Grant shortcuts are not constrained to 2 unique characters, so issued IDs cannot be decoded
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() is documented as "usually like 3-letters", but the encoder writes the shortcut as-is and getTokenContextFromTokenId requires the prefix before ':' to be exactly 6 characters (2+2+2) and throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise. postInit stores whatever getShortcut() returns and only compares map sizes, so a 1-character, 3-character, empty, or colon-containing shortcut still starts the server and is embedded in new access-token IDs. Those tokens cannot be parsed by the same provider. The lazy refresh in getShortcutByGrantType (around line 113) and getGrantTypeByShortcut is worse: on a cache miss it puts the new shortcut into both maps with no length check and no uniqueness check, so a hot-deployed grant can overwrite another grant's shortcut. Decoding then either throws or reports the wrong grant type. Validate at registration and on the lazy path that every shortcut is exactly two characters, contains no ':', and is not already mapped to a different grant; fix the javadoc to match.

findings.title: Unset grant type is silently encoded as na on issuance paths this PR did not update
findings.body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext treats a missing ClientSessionContext Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute as the shortcut na, and encodeTokenId will persist that into the access-token jti. This PR only sets the attribute in OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, the ROPC and pre-authorized grants, StandardTokenExchangeProvider, and the refresh path in TokenManager.validateToken. Other callers of TokenManager.initToken / createClientAccessToken are unchanged. Implicit and hybrid access tokens are issued from the authorization endpoint, not the token endpoint, and legacy token-exchange providers other than StandardTokenExchangeProvider are not in this diff. Those tokens are minted with grant shortcut na even though the grant is known. Once introspection or session lookup trusts the encoded grant (the stated reason for this change), those tokens take the unknown-grant path and the optimization is wrong. Every access-token issuance path needs to set the real grant, or initToken must fail instead of writing na for a request whose grant is known.

findings.title: Decode error claims the whole token ID must be length 6
findings.body: When the prefix before ':' is not 6 characters, the exception says Incorrect token id: '<full id>'. Expected length of 6. The full jti is a 6-character prefix plus ':' plus a UUID, so the message describes the wrong length and will send operators looking at the wrong field when decode starts failing requests.
